categoryMeta.description: Race-week, taper, pre-race, and sharpening workouts across different race distances.

workouts.title: 5K Race Week 3 × 1K Controlled
workouts.summary: A low-volume 5K race-week session to rehearse rhythm without building fatigue.
workouts.riskReason: Race-rhythm work can create fatigue if run too fast; recoveries and volume are intentionally conservative.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run by relaxed race rhythm or easy effort. This session should sharpen, not test fitness.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate may rise during short faster work, but overall session load should stay low.

warmup.name: Easy Jog
warmup.description: Run easy to raise core temperature before the quality work.
notes: Keep this relaxed and conversational.

warmup.name: Dynamic Prep
warmup.description: Complete light dynamic mobility: leg swings, ankle circles, skips, and relaxed running drills.
notes: Move smoothly without forcing range of motion.

warmup.name: Relaxed Strides
warmup.description: Run relaxed strides to prepare rhythm and turnover.
notes: Finish feeling sharper, not tired.

mainSet.name: 3 × 1K Controlled 5K Rhythm
mainSet.description: Run 3 repetitions of 1000m at controlled 5K race effort.
notes: Keep each repetition controlled and repeatable.

cooldown.name: Easy Cooldown Jog
cooldown.description: Jog easily after the main set to bring heart rate down gradually.
notes: Extend the cooldown if legs feel heavy.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 2 × 1K Controlled 5K Rhythm
mainSet.description: Run 2 repetitions of 1000m at controlled 5K race effort.
notes: Keep each repetition controlled and repeatable.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 4 × 1K Controlled 5K Rhythm
mainSet.description: Run 4 repetitions of 1000m at controlled 5K race effort.
notes: Keep each repetition controlled and repeatable.

coachingNotes: Leave the workout feeling fresher than when you started.
Do not chase a personal best in race week training.
Cut the session short if legs feel unusually flat, tight, or painful.
commonMistakes: Turning a taper session into a fitness test.
Adding extra reps because the workout feels short.
Running the first repetition too hard and creating unnecessary fatigue.
safetyNotes: Do not perform this workout through sharp pain or unusual tightness.
Keep recovery generous and stop if mechanics deteriorate.
Use the easier variant if the race is close or fatigue is high.

shareCard.purposeText: A low-volume 5K race-week session to rehearse rhythm without building fatigue.

workouts.riskReason: Low volume and controlled intensity keep fatigue and injury risk low during race week.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run by relaxed race rhythm or easy effort. This session should sharpen, not test fitness.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate may rise during short faster work, but overall session load should stay low.

warmup.name: Gentle Mobility
warmup.description: Use light mobility or walking before the short shakeout.
notes: Keep it minimal and relaxed.

mainSet.name: 20-Min Very Easy Shakeout
mainSet.description: Run continuously for 20 minutes at very easy effort.
notes: Start controlled and settle into rhythm.

cooldown.name: Easy Walk-Jog Cooldown
cooldown.description: Walk or jog very easily after the main endurance work.
notes: Rehydrate and let breathing return to normal.

easier.description: Reduce the main-set load while keeping the same training purpose.

mainSet.name: 15-Min Very Easy Shakeout
mainSet.description: Run continuously for 15 minutes at very easy effort.
notes: Start controlled and settle into rhythm.

harder.description: Increase the main-set load only when the base version is controlled.

mainSet.name: 25-Min Very Easy Shakeout
mainSet.description: Run continuously for 25 minutes at very easy effort.
notes: Start controlled and settle into rhythm.

coachingNotes: Leave the workout feeling fresher than when you started.
Do not chase a personal best in race week training.
Cut the session short if legs feel unusually flat, tight, or painful.
commonMistakes: Turning a taper session into a fitness test.
Adding extra reps because the workout feels short.
Running the first repetition too hard and creating unnecessary fatigue.
safetyNotes: Do not perform this workout through sharp pain or unusual tightness.
Keep recovery generous and stop if mechanics deteriorate.
Use the easier variant if the race is close or fatigue is high.
